newsitem.title: UK: British worker wins record RSI damages.
newsitem.headline: British worker wins record RSI damages.

text.p: A machine operator has won record damages for Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) in Britain, her union announced on Thursday.
Muriel Simpson, 42, retired on grounds of ill-health in 1990 from her factory job in Cumbria, northern England, and will never be able to do manual work again.
She was awarded damages of 186,000 pounds ($304,000), a record for an RSI case, after a four-day hearing in the northeastern English city of Newcastle.

RSI affects up to 200,000 workers every year, according to a recent union survey. The disorder mainly affects workers who use computer keyboards and is usually characterised by swelling, muscular spasm and tenderness in joints and ligaments.
Simpson suffered pains in her arm when she worked on a toilet-paper making machine between 1987 and 1990.
She received medical treatment for her condition, which the union said became "chronic", and sued for negligence and breach of health and safety laws. Her company denied negligence.
